items.prompt: Which word in the poem rhymes with play?
hints: Rhyming words sound the same at the end.
Say play, then say each word.
Look at the end of the first part of the poem.
items.explanation: Today and play rhyme. They both end with the sound ay.

options.why: Rain does not sound like play at the end.
Roof ends with a different sound.

items.prompt: Where does the rain fall at the start of the poem?
hints: Read the first line.
Find the word on.
Read the words after Pitter, patter.
items.explanation: The first line says the rain falls on the roof.

options.why: The frogs are in the puddle later.
Rain does not fall on the sun.

hints: Some words sound like the noise they name.
Say each one out loud.
Which one sounds like water falling?
items.explanation: Drip, drop sounds like rain falling. Pitter, patter does too.

options.why: These are things the child will do.
These words do not sound like rain.

items.prompt: Match the rhyming words from the poem.
hints: Say the words out loud.
Rhyming words sound the same at the end.
Start with today. Which word sounds like it?
items.explanation: Today rhymes with play, and about rhymes with shout.

items.prompt: How does the child feel at the end of the poem?
hints: Read the last two lines.
What will the child do when the sun comes back?
How do you feel when you run and shout?
items.explanation: When the sun comes back, the child will run and shout. That shows the child is excited.

options.why: The child is sad when it rains. Look at the end.
Nothing in the poem is scary.

items.prompt: What does the child dig with?
hints: Find the word dig.
Read the rest of that line.
Look in the middle part of the poem.
items.explanation: The poem says: I dig with my spade.

options.why: The poem does not say a shell.
The poem does not say a stick.

hints: Find the word feet in the poem.
Look at the next line.
Say feet, then say the last word of the next line.
items.explanation: Feet and heat rhyme because they end with the same sound.

options.why: Sand ends with a different sound.
Sun ends with a different sound.

hints: Two answers are right.
Read the poem slowly.
Look for living things that move.
items.explanation: The poem has a crab and some birds.

options.why: There are no fish in the poem.
There is no dog in the poem.

items.prompt: Why does the crab run away?
hints: Find the word crab.
Read the line after the crab runs away.
What does the poem say the crab wants?
items.explanation: The poem says the crab runs away because it does not want to play.

options.why: The poem does not say this.

options.text: It does not want to play.

options.why: The poem says the sun gives heat.

items.prompt: Finish the line from the poem. 'When the day is done, I wave to the ___.'
hints: Look at the last part of the poem.
The missing word rhymes with done.
It is something hot in the sky.
items.explanation: The poem ends: I wave to the sun. Sun rhymes with done.

hints: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Say cat, then say each word.
Listen to the end: at.
items.explanation: Cat and hat rhyme. They both end with at.

options.why: Cup ends with a different sound.
Dog ends with a different sound.

items.prompt: Does it rhyme with bee? Sort the words.
hints: Say bee, then say each word.
Listen to the end sound.
Start with tree. Does it end like bee?
items.explanation: Tree, sea and three rhyme with bee. Bed, bag and cup do not.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that rhyme with cake.
hints: Three words are right.
Say cake, then say each word.
Listen for the ake sound at the end.
items.explanation: Lake, make and snake rhyme with cake.

options.why: Cat ends with a different sound.
Kite ends with a different sound.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT rhyme with the others?
hints: Say all four words.
Three words end the same way.
Listen to the middle sound too.
items.explanation: Ball, tall and wall rhyme. Bell has an e sound in the middle, so it does not rhyme with them.

options.why: Ball rhymes with tall and wall.
Tall rhymes with ball and wall.
Wall rhymes with ball and tall.

items.prompt: Which pair rhymes, but ends with different letters?
hints: All four pairs rhyme.
Now look at the spelling at the end of each word.
Find the pair where the last letters are not the same.
items.explanation: Blue and shoe rhyme, but blue ends with ue and shoe ends with oe.

options.why: These end with the same letters, at.
These end with the same letters, ig.
These end with the same letters, un.
